children: The expanded tie up with Nothing’s CMF brand will bring manufacturing, ownership and smartphone research and development under a broader India focused structure

Optiemus Infracom shares hit the 20 per cent upper circuit at Rs 708.40 on the BSE on Tuesday, 22 September, after the company expanded its partnership with Nothing Electronics for CMF, driving a sharp increase in trading volumes. The development will deepen Optiemus’s role in CMF’s manufacturing, ownership and research and development (R&D) activities in India, with the partnership targeting an end to end smartphone capability.

By 1.32 p.m., more than 8.55 million Optiemus Infracom shares had changed hands across the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and BSE, while average trading volumes were more than 20 times higher than usual, according to market data. Pending buy orders across the two exchanges stood at about 1.22 million shares.

CMF, the consumer technology brand of Nothing, has expanded its partnership with the Optiemus Group as it seeks to establish a stronger India based technology and manufacturing base. As part of the arrangement, Optiemus will participate in Nothing’s upcoming Series A investment round for CMF.

The move is intended to put CMF on a path towards becoming a majority Indian owned and independent smartphone brand, while increasing the role of India beyond manufacturing to product development and engineering.

The expanded arrangement builds on the strategic manufacturing joint venture between Nothing and Optiemus announced in September 2025. That partnership established India as a production hub for Nothing and CMF devices.

Under the expanded structure, the companies plan to bring manufacturing, ownership and R&D capabilities together within an India focused entity. The objective is to increase local design and engineering capabilities and strengthen India's position in the smartphone value chain.

The development also comes as Optiemus continues to expand its presence across India's electronics and mobility ecosystem. The company, founded in 1993, operates across manufacturing, distribution and retailing of mobile and telecommunications products.
The sharp movement in Optiemus shares followed the partnership development, with the stock reaching its upper trading limit amid heavy volumes on Tuesday.
